name: 高中物理可视化
description: 2D physics engine for Chinese high-school physics with AI scene JSON + canvas visualization.

zh.name: 高中物理可视化
zh.description: 覆盖高中物理力学/振动波动/电磁/光学/热学/近代物理的 2D 可视化；AI 输出 scene JSON 并驱动播放。

en.name: High-school Physics
en.description: 2D visualizer covering Chinese high-school physics; AI outputs scene JSON and drives playback.

tools.name: phys_validate
tools.description: Validate a physics scene JSON against the schema. Returns {ok, errors[]}. Always validate before phys_load; on failure, fix the JSON and retry.

tools.name: phys_load
tools.description: Load a physics scene JSON into the visualizer (opens the panel). Scene fields: topic, zh, world{xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax,air}, g, bodies[{id,x,y,vx,vy,mass,radius,q,color,label,fixed,bounce,e,mu,mu0}], springs[{a,b,k,rest,damping}], fields[{type:'E',Ex,Ey | mag,angle | U,d,angle}, {type:'B',Bz | mag,dir:'out'|'in'}], walls[{x1,y1,x2,y2,bounce,mu,mu0}], planet{G,M,R}, modules[{kind,<params>}] (kinds: projectile,incline,circular,pendulum,spring,collision,gravitation,shm,wave,plates,circuit,transformer,induction,refraction,lens,mirror,gas,photoelectric,decay — call phys_list_params for every parameter, unit and range), optics{rays,mirrors,lenses,interfaces}, circuit{type:'RC'|'AC',...}, plots[{id,of:'body.prop'}], dt. Coordinates: +x right, +y up; gravity pulls -y. NEW (v3.4.0) element-library scenes: elements[{id,type,x,y,angle,<type params>}] — 54 element types (block, ball, cylinder, rod, wedge, polygon, ring, ground, wall, incline, arc, loop, conveyor, pulley, rope, lightRod, spring, cord, hinge, plank, cart, turntable, launcher, fieldE, fieldB, rails, coil, lens, mirror, prism, glass, photogate, readout…); use phys_list_element_types for every type, parameter, unit and range, and phys_add_element / phys_update_element to build scenes incrementally. Element scenes use real rigid-body simulation (friction, rolling, belts, pulleys, ropes) and are editable in the panel (palette, inspector, handles).

tools.name: phys_play
tools.description: Play the current physics simulation.

tools.name: phys_pause
tools.description: Pause the physics simulation.

tools.name: phys_step
tools.description: Advance a few simulation steps while paused.

tools.name: phys_reset
tools.description: Reset the scene to its initial state.

tools.name: phys_set_speed
tools.description: Set playback speed (0.25–4).

tools.name: phys_state
tools.description: Read current simulation state (t, body positions/velocities, circuit).

tools.name: phys_list_examples
tools.description: List built-in example scenes covering Chinese high-school physics topics.

tools.name: phys_load_example
tools.description: Load a built-in example by id (from phys_list_examples).

tools.name: phys_set_param
tools.description: Set ONE parameter and apply live. Module scene: {module:0,key:'v0',value:20} (or path 'modules[0].v0'; aliases such as frequency/speed/wavelength work). Body scene: dotted path e.g. bodies[0].mass, g, world.air, springs[0].k, fields[0].mag, walls[0].mu0. Out-of-range values return an error with the allowed range.

tools.name: phys_update
tools.description: Update several parameters at once: {changes:{'modules[0].v0':20,'modules[0].angle':30}} or a single {path|key,value}. Same validation as phys_set_param.

tools.name: phys_list_params
tools.description: List every customisable parameter of the loaded module scene (key, Chinese name, unit, min, max, enum, current value) and all module kinds. Call this before phys_set_param when unsure of a key.

tools.name: phys_add_element
tools.description: Add one element from the physics element library to the current scene (creates a blank sandbox scene if none is loaded; converts a simple legacy scene). `type` is an element type id from phys_list_element_types (e.g. block, ball, conveyor, pulley, rope, rails, lens, loop, fieldB, massSpectrometer…) or a custom type defined with phys_define_custom_element. `props` holds the parameters (x, y, angle in degrees, mass, mu0, mu, …; units/ranges from phys_list_element_types; ropes/springs/hinges reference elements by id with a/b and local anchors ax,ay,bx,by). Returns {ok,id,ids} or {ok:false,errors[]} — errors name the bad parameter and its allowed range; fix and retry. Template types (massSpectrometer, cyclotron) expand to several elements (ids returned). Coordinates: +x right, +y up, metres, degrees counter-clockwise.

props.description: parameters of the element (may also be given at top level)

tools.name: phys_update_element
tools.description: Change parameters of an existing element by id (position, size, mass, friction, field strength, refractive index, …). Values are validated against the type's ranges; live-safe parameters (labels, colours, belt speed, field strength…) apply to a running simulation without resetting it, geometric changes rebuild the scene at t=0. Returns {ok,applied} or {ok:false,errors[]}.

tools.name: phys_remove_element
tools.description: Remove an element by id. Elements that depend on it (ropes, springs, hinges, readouts attached to it) are removed too; the result lists everything removed.

tools.name: phys_list_element_types
tools.description: List the element library: every element type with id, Chinese/English name, category (shape, surface, mech, field, optic, meas, mine), description and every parameter with key, unit, min, max, default and options, plus the user's custom types. Optionally filter by category. Call this before phys_add_element when unsure of a parameter name or range.

category.description: shape | surface | mech | field | optic | meas | mine

tools.name: phys_define_custom_element
tools.description: Define a reusable custom element type (saved in the user's 我的元件 library). Either {id, zh, base:'<built-in type>', defaults:{param:value…}} for a preset of one type (e.g. a heavy block), or {id, zh, template:[{type,id?,x,y,…params}…]} for a group of elements placed relative to the drop point (ref params may use template ids). Then phys_add_element with type=<id>. Returns {ok,id} or {ok:false,errors[]}.

tools.name: phys_new_scene
tools.description: Start a blank element-library sandbox scene (replaces the current scene). Optional topic, zh title, g, world{xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax}.

tools.name: phys_get_elements
tools.description: Return all elements of the current element scene (their parameters), plus live runtime values (positions, velocities, readouts) and build warnings.
